issues.description: The problem statement contains conflicting signatures for messageOnMilk. The UML and the rest of the code expect a no-argument method messageOnMilk(): String, but a later paragraph in the problem text instructs students to implement messageOnMilk(double milkVolume). This parameter mismatch is inconsistent with the template (which calls messageOnMilk() with no args) and with the provided solution, and will confuse students and cause compile/test failures if they implement the double-parameter version.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the contradiction in the problem statement: either (A) remove the double-parameter example and explicitly require messageOnMilk(): String (matching the UML, template Main calls, and solution), or (B) change the UML, template, and solution to use messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) everywhere (and update all calls such as in Main and tests). Prefer option (A) if tests and template expect a no-arg method.

issues.description: The problem description requires a method messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) (including a milkVolume parameter and specific return format), but the provided template usage and the solution define messageOnMilk() without any parameter. This mismatch in the method signature (presence vs. absence of the double parameter) creates confusion for students about the required API and expected output format.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the API consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement to require messageOnMilk() with no parameters and remove the volume-based return format, or (B) update the interface and implementations to declare messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and adjust all call sites (e.g., Main and tests) to pass a double value. If choosing option B, also update implementations to return the specified format: "[Animal Type] [name] is milked (volume: [milkVolume]L)".
